Original Requirements: Develop a prototype Smart House system (DigitalHome) to manage temperature, humidity, security, and appliance power via a web interface. The system includes a Gateway, sensors (thermostats, humidistats, contact switches), and controllers. It must support remote monitoring, scheduling, reporting, and user management within a 12-month timeline by a 5-engineer team, using a simulated environment to aid business decisions for future commercial development.
Product Goals: Validate business viability through a functional prototype within 12 months
Enable seamless remote monitoring and control of home environment via web
Ensure high system reliability, security, and data backup mechanisms
User Stories: As a General User, I want to monitor temperature and humidity via a web page so I can ensure home comfort.
As a General User, I want to set schedules for appliances and climate so I can automate my home environment.
As a Master User, I want to configure user accounts and system parameters so I can manage access rights.
As a Technician, I want to backup and recover system data so I can maintain system integrity during failures.
As a General User, I want to receive security alerts when breaches occur so I can protect my home.
Competitive Analysis: Google Nest: Comprehensive ecosystem, high cost, strong brand recognition
Samsung SmartThings: Wide device compatibility, complex setup for non-tech users
Home Assistant: Open source, high customization, high technical barrier
Amazon Alexa Smart Home: Voice-centric integration, privacy concerns for some users
Apple HomeKit: High security standards, limited device support, expensive ecosystem
Honeywell Home: Strong HVAC focus, less comprehensive appliance control
DigitalHome Prototype: Cost-effective, focused on core metrics, simulated environment for validation

Requirement Analysis: The project requires a web-based central management system connected to a Gateway device via broadband. Key functional requirements include environmental control (temp/humidity), security monitoring (contact sensors/alarms), and appliance management (power switches). Non-functional requirements emphasize reliability (1 failure per 10,000 hours), security (TLS encryption), and data backup. Constraints include a 12-month timeline, 5-engineer team, minimized costs, and usage of a simulated environment for testing. The system must support multiple user roles (General, Master, Technician) and provide reporting features.
Requirement Pool: Implement DigitalHome Gateway with RF module for wireless communication with sensors/controllers
Develop web server interface for remote monitoring and control of devices
Implement user authentication and data encryption (TLS) for security
Create scheduling system for thermostats, humidistats, and power switches
Develop backup and recovery mechanism for system data and configurations
UI Design draft: Web-based dashboard accessible via computer or mobile. Layout includes a main navigation bar (Climate, Security, Appliances, Reports). Climate section shows real-time temp/humidity gauges with set-point sliders. Security section displays sensor status (Open/Closed) and alarm toggle. Appliances section lists switches with ON/OFF toggles. Reports section provides monthly graphs and logs. Style should be clean, responsive, and update data at least every 2 seconds.
Anything UNCLEAR: Specific hardware models for sensors and controllers are not defined, only functional specs. The exact RF protocol (e.g., Zigbee, Z-Wave, Proprietary) is not specified. The fidelity of the 'simulated environment' regarding physical properties needs clarification to ensure valid testing results. Detailed budget constraints beyond 'minimized cost' are not quantified.
